chapter: Joseph Thomas band and house parties
title: Joseph Thomas band and its picnics
summary: After the two-piece jobs Williams joined Joseph Thomas, whose band played more picnics than any in the city; he describes the trucks, pavilion halls, ticket prices and refreshments.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well after you played those little two piece jobs, who did you get with then?
You mean who did I went with?
Yeah, what band did you go with then?
Went with then, I went with Joseph Thomas.
You said something about picnics too, you played picnics.
Yeah, well we played, we broke the record in picnics. We had more picnics than any band in the city of New Orleans.
Well what happens at a picnic like that? Is it out of doors or indoors?

No, it's something in the pavilion. Out on the pavilion they got halls, you know. And down at that time there wasn't no buses, there was trucks. You know, they'd have trucks and clubs and Thomas was working for Solara then. And Solara gave one of the biggest picnics, you know. And then we was connected with the K&B, Catherine Bestra's employees. And there used to be what and what, but they never was on the same day.
And would they go out in the country?

Yeah, go out in the country, go out to La Plaste, maybe they might go to, go to Arlington, across the river, you know. They went to different places, they never went to the same place. They went to La Vida Spring, Pas Christiane, they went to different places. Go down to Sebastopol.
What would they do at one of those, you know, before I ever came to town?

Well, all they did, you pay your fare, say the tickets might be a dollar round trip. That dollar round trip, it admits you in the hall. And if you didn't have a ticket, it was then at that door when they get there with the van and things, you'd have to pay fifty cents to come in if you didn't sneak in. Because a lot of people had their own cars, you know, automobiles, go along and they call. And then they sell their refreshments and stuff. Some people bring their refreshments to get out on the lawn, you know, in the yard, different things. Some of them get up on the levee banks. And then the rest of them will be up in there dancing.
What kind of refreshments would they have?
Oh, they'd have all kinds of, eat sandwiches, you know, and beer, whiskey. Wine selling just like a drink.
Yeah, they sell it, they come.
You could bring your own basket if you wanted.
Yeah, yeah, most of them bring their baskets. Yeah, they bring their baskets.
